title: Why some neurons fall silent in Alzheimer’s disease
body: New in PNAS: in mouse models of β-amyloidosis, silent neurons lose much of their presynaptic input and many dendritic spines — synaptic decoupling as a mechanism behind the decline of neuronal activity.

title: Our lab on 3sat “nano”: Diagnose Alzheimer-Demenz
body: The science programme nano (3sat) featured our research in its episode on Alzheimer’s disease research — the lab appears in the first five minutes of the broadcast.

title: Stopping Alzheimer’s-related hyperactivity at an early stage
body: In Nature Communications we show that an anticalin protein that scavenges β-amyloid monomers suppresses early neuronal hyperactivity and synaptic glutamate accumulation in the APP23xPS45 mouse model — but only before plaques form. TUM published a press release on the study.

title: A vicious cycle of β-amyloid-dependent hyperactivation
body: Published in Science: β-amyloid causes neuronal hyperactivation by blocking glutamate reuptake, preferentially in neurons that are already active — a mechanism that can operate before plaques appear.
